note: Whitelist for §3.2 universality claims. An agent may cite a theorem ONLY by an id in this file, and must state how its technique's hypotheses map onto the theorem's. A theorem an agent merely names from memory is an LLM assertion, which §3.2 explicitly does not accept. Adding an entry is a human decision made in a reviewed diff, not something an agent does mid-run.

theorems.name: Division algorithm
theorems.statement: For integers a and b with b > 0 there exist unique integers q, r such that a = bq + r and 0 <= r < b.
theorems.source: Standard; e.g. Hardy & Wright, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers, Thm 1.

theorems.name: Digit-sum congruence in base b
theorems.statement: For an integer n with base-b digits d_k...d_0, n is congruent to the sum of its digits modulo (b - 1).
theorems.source: Immediate from b ≡ 1 (mod b-1). Standard result underlying casting out nines.

theorems.name: Fermat's little theorem
theorems.statement: If p is prime and p does not divide a, then a^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p).

theorems.name: Euler's theorem
theorems.statement: If gcd(a, n) = 1 then a^phi(n) ≡ 1 (mod n).

theorems.name: Chinese remainder theorem
theorems.statement: If n_1..n_k are pairwise coprime, the system x ≡ a_i (mod n_i) has a unique solution modulo the product of the n_i.

theorems.name: Binomial theorem
theorems.statement: (x + y)^n = sum over k of C(n,k) x^(n-k) y^k, for non-negative integer n.
hypotheses: x, y in a commutative ring

theorems.name: Difference of squares
theorems.statement: a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b) in any commutative ring.
hypotheses: a, b in a commutative ring

theorems.name: AM–GM inequality
theorems.statement: For non-negative reals, the arithmetic mean is at least the geometric mean, with equality iff all values are equal.
theorems.source: Standard; Hardy, Littlewood & Pólya, Inequalities, Thm 9.

theorems.name: Pythagorean theorem
theorems.statement: In a Euclidean right triangle with legs a, b and hypotenuse c, a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

theorems.name: Sum of an arithmetic progression
theorems.statement: The sum of n terms of an arithmetic progression with first term a and last term l is n(a + l)/2.
